Fewer denoising steps are better — on every geometry metric

The same trained flow checkpoint, sampled with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 20 ODE steps. The arm trains and evaluates at 20 steps, yet 20 is the worst setting of the five. Error rises monotonically with step count.

2 steps beats the 20-step default by 22.2%. The largest gap of any metric.
Best overall setting
2 steps
Wins LossPointmap and LossRaymap. 1 step wins MSEToken and LossDepth.
The shape of the result. 1 step is the pure regression baseline — it emits x̂(noise, t=0) with no integration at all — and it already beats the 20-step sampler everywhere. Extra ODE steps do not refine the sample; they walk it away from the target.

LossFlow · a different t in every pass
Why it cannot be read

Each pass drew its own timesteps

flow_noising took t from the global RNG while the eval generator seeded only the noise. Five passes in one process = five different t sets. Since fixed with a dedicated _eval_t_gen, which leaves the decoded metrics byte-unchanged.

Reading it — what this changes, and what it does not

The sampler is not buying anything on this arm

A 1-step forward pass matches or beats a 20-step ODE integration on all five metrics, at 1/20th the sampling cost. That is a statement about this checkpoint, not about flow matching in general. Mechanism: docs/analysis/deltatok_flow_numsteps_why_more_steps_degrade.md.

Takeaway

Evaluate at 1–2 steps, not 20

Switching the eval default from 20 to 2 steps improves LossRaymap 22%, LossPointmap 15% and MSEToken 13%, and cuts eval sampling cost 10×. Nothing about training changes.

Interpretation

Two effects pulling the same way

Any working sampler loses to its own mean on a distortion metric, so a rise is expected. On top of that t_dist=uniform with the v-weighting leaves 0.28% of the loss mass below t=0.1, so the 1-step readout is also the least-trained point of the model.

Caveats

What this does not establish

  • One seed, one arm. tc128 compose at ep100 only. No repeat, no other width.
  • ODE mode only. The damped sampler was not run in this sweep.
  • Steps > 20 untested here. The trend is measured over 1–20; 50 and 100 were not sampled on this arm.
  • LossFlow is unusable here. Each pass drew its own t, so that column is RNG. Fixed in the trainer; the sweep was not re-run.
  • Per-frame L1 is noisy. Of the 4 val sequences drawn at t4, only one reproduces the monotone ordering.
Cross-arm comparison is missing. An equivalent 1,20,50,75,100 sweep exists for the tc768 arm (slurm/eval_deltatok_flow_numsteps_tc768_bsc.slurm), but its results are not in monitor_jobs.json or archived_jobs.json and were not recovered.
